name: Content Aggregator
author: relisiuol

sections.description:
Your sources publish all day. Your site should keep up.

Content Aggregator turns the sites, feeds and social accounts you follow into WordPress posts, automatically. Paste an address, check the preview, and new articles reach your site every 15 minutes: as drafts you review, or as posts published for you.

No account, no API key, no code. The plugin talks to the sources you add and to nothing else, and it is complete as it is: no locked feature, no cap on sources or posts.

Made for

  • News and niche sites that cover a subject from many sources.
  • Curation sites and link blogs that publish the best of what they read.
  • Agencies, networks and communities that show the latest posts of their clients, partners or members.
  • Any site that wants a “latest from my sources” list on a page, without creating a single post.

Up and running in a minute

  1. Open Content Aggregator > Sources > Add and paste the address of a site or a feed.
  2. Click Test source to see the posts it would create.
  3. Save. The first import starts within seconds, and new items arrive as drafts.
  4. Publish them from Posts, or add the Latest from your sources block to a page to list them without creating posts.

Everything you get, free

  • Sources found from an address. Paste the URL of a site, a YouTube channel, a subreddit, a Bluesky profile or a Mastodon account: the feed and its format are detected for you.
  • A preview before anything is imported. “Test source” shows the posts a source would create, so nothing lands on your site by surprise.
  • Imports that run themselves. From every 15 minutes to once a day, in the background, never while a visitor waits. An “Import now” button on each source for when you cannot wait.
  • Posts shaped your way. Draft, pending or published. Categories, a featured image taken from the article or a default one per source, and templates for the title, the date and the content.
  • Real blocks, not pasted HTML. Imported content is converted to WordPress blocks whenever it can be, so it edits like a post written on your site.
  • No double imports. An article is imported once, even when its publisher retitles it or two of your sources carry it.
  • Credit where it is due. Templates can link every post to its source, and a post can send its readers straight to the original article.
  • A block and a shortcode. List the latest items of your sources anywhere, in columns, with thumbnails, excerpts, authors, keyword filters and pages.
  • Sources that look after themselves. Each one shows when it was last read and why it last failed, a source that stays silent can be switched off for you, and the import log and Site Health say what happened.
  • Your own parsers. Any JSON or XML source becomes one of yours, set up from the admin with a preview, with custom request headers and query parameters for the sources that need them.
  • Multisite ready, with sources, settings and an import log for each site, and translated into French.

Supported sources

  • RSS and Atom feeds, and WordPress sites.
  • YouTube channels (from their /channel/… address) and playlists, subreddits, GitHub repositories and Medium profiles: paste the page address and its feed is found.
  • Bluesky profiles, Mastodon hashtags and accounts, and Hacker News lists.
  • Any other JSON or XML source, with a parser you define.

Show your sources anywhere

The Latest from your sources block, or the [content_aggregator_items] shortcode on classic themes, lists the latest items of your sources, newest first, each linking to the original article. Choose the sources, the number of items and of columns, what each item shows, and the words that keep an item in or leave it out.

Example: [content_aggregator_items count="8" columns="2" show_excerpt="true"]. Every option is listed in the FAQ.

Templates

Each source can shape the title, the date and the content of its posts with placeholders such as __TITLE__, __CONTENT__ and __URL__, and actions such as truncate or strip HTML, picked from a menu.

Go further with Content Aggregator Pro

Importing is half of the work. Content Aggregator Pro, a separate paid add-on, turns what your sources publish into articles of your own:

  • Stories, not items. The same news told by ten outlets becomes one story, ranked on trust, coverage and freshness, with the reasons shown.
  • Articles in your voice. Pro writes a complete WordPress article in your language, your voice and your tone. Every source is linked, and what could not be verified is flagged for your review.
  • As much automation as you want. Approve each draft yourself, let Pro create the drafts for you, or let it publish, always inside the limits you set: articles per day, quiet hours, minimum score, keywords, sources and a monthly budget. One button stops everything.
  • Results for each article. Record them by hand, or connect Google Analytics 4, Matomo, Plausible or Google Search Console.

Pro installs next to this plugin and works through its own online service, with a licence. This plugin never contacts that service, and does everything listed above it without Pro. Plans and pricing: https://content-aggregator.relisiuol.fr/#pricing

For developers

Actions and filters surround every import, a source and its posts can be extended from another plugin, and the source code, with its build steps, is at https://github.com/relisiuol/content-aggregator

External services

Content Aggregator contacts the sources you add, and nothing else. Your site’s server requests their addresses (feeds, REST API endpoints, and, when you add such a source, the public APIs of Bluesky and Mastodon servers, and Algolia’s search API for Hacker News lists), and they receive what any web request carries: its address, your server’s IP address and a User-Agent. Each source’s own terms and privacy policy apply.

When the block or the shortcode shows images, your server fetches each image once from its source and serves its own copy.

Development

The source code, with its build steps, is at https://github.com/relisiuol/content-aggregator
sections.installation:
1. In the WordPress admin, go to Plugins > Add New, search for “Content Aggregator”, then click Install Now and Activate.
  2. Open the new Content Aggregator menu and follow the quick start above.
  3. Under Settings, choose how often sources are checked.
sections.faq:
Is it really free?

Yes. Every source type, the schedule, the templates, the block, the shortcode and your own parsers are in this plugin, with no cap on sources or posts and nothing to unlock.

Which sources can I import?

RSS and Atom feeds, WordPress sites, YouTube channels and playlists, subreddits, GitHub repositories, Medium profiles, Bluesky profiles, Mastodon hashtags and accounts, Hacker News lists, and any JSON or XML source with a parser you define. Pasting the address of a page usually finds its feed.

Are imported posts published right away?

Only if you choose so. New sources create drafts, and you set the status for each source.

Will I get duplicate posts?

The plugin remembers every item it has read, so an article is imported once, even when its title changes or two sources carry it.

Are images imported?

Yes. An item’s image becomes the featured image of its post when the feed provides one; otherwise the default image of the source is used.

Does it slow my site down?

Imports run in the background, a few sources at a time, never while a visitor waits.

Imports are late on a quiet site. Why?

WordPress runs its scheduled tasks when the site is visited. On a quiet site, ask your host to run the WordPress scheduler on a timer, or use “Import now” on a source.

Can I republish what I import?

You choose your sources, so make sure you may reuse their content. An imported post can also redirect to the original article.

Does it send data anywhere?

Only requests to the sources you add, from your own server. See “External services” below.

Does it work on multisite?

Yes. Each site of a network has its own sources, settings and import log.

A source does not import. What should I check?

Open the source: its last failure and the reason are on its edit screen and in the Import log. “Test source” shows what the plugin reads.

Which options does the shortcode take?

[content_aggregator_items] takes:

  • count: number of items, 1 to 50 (default 5).
  • sources: source numbers separated by commas; empty for all of them.
  • columns: 1 to 4 (default 1).
  • show_source, show_date: true or false (default true).
  • show_excerpt, show_image, show_author: true or false (default false).
  • excerpt_length: words, 5 to 60 (default 25).
  • include, exclude: words separated by commas, to keep or leave out the items that mention them.
  • order: newest (default), oldest, title or source.
  • per_page: items per page, with “Previous” and “Next” links; 0 for a single list (default).
  • new_tab, nofollow: true or false (default false).

The block has the same options in its settings panel.

Can developers extend it?

Yes. Parsers are set up from the admin, and the actions and filters around each import are documented at https://github.com/relisiuol/content-aggregator

What does Content Aggregator Pro add?

Content Aggregator Pro is a separate paid add-on: it groups related articles into stories, ranks them, and writes articles from them in your voice, which you approve one by one or let it publish within limits you set. “Go further with Content Aggregator Pro”, in the description, has the details. The free plugin is complete on its own.
sections.changelog:
2.2.0 – 2026-11-17

New

  • “Latest from your sources” block and [content_aggregator_items] shortcode: list the latest items anywhere, with columns, excerpts, thumbnails, authors, keyword filters, ordering and pages.
  • Paste the address of a YouTube channel or playlist, a subreddit, a GitHub repository, a Medium profile, a Bluesky profile, a Mastodon hashtag or account, or a Hacker News list: its feed is found for you.
  • Parsers you define from the admin for JSON and XML sources.
  • A preview of the posts a source would create, before anything is imported.
  • “Import now” on each source, and a first import that starts as soon as a source is enabled.
  • Title and content templates composed with chips, with actions such as truncate, replace and strip HTML.
  • Custom request headers and query parameters for the sources that need them.
  • Import log views by outcome, Site Health checks and a diagnostic report to copy into a support request.
  • A panel that administrators can dismiss presents Content Aggregator Pro.

Improved

  • New sources create drafts by default, and new installs check their sources every 15 minutes. Existing sites keep their settings.
  • An article is imported once, even when its publisher retitles or redates it, or when two sources carry it.
  • Each source shows when it was last read, when it last produced an item and why it last failed, and the list has views and filters.
  • Images served without a file extension are imported, and feeds that declare the wrong encoding are read correctly.
  • A source can be saved without categories or a default image.
  • The new screens are translated into French.

Security

  • The certificate path is checked more strictly, and XML feeds are parsed without network access.

Fixed

  • Uninstalling removes the plugin’s data on every site of a network.
  • Imported posts are attributed to an administrator or, without one, to a user who can publish.
  • Admin fixes: a blank page after adding a source, the list search, forms that lost what was typed, PHP 8.4 notices.

2.1.3 – 2026-05-02

  • Declare compatibility with WordPress 6.9
  • Improve auto-detection and parser registry support, including Atom feeds
  • Fix parser validation and XML namespace handling regressions
  • Harden CI linting and release checks
  • Add WordPress.org directory assets and Playground blueprint

2.0.0 – 2025-08-21

  • Add labels to settings fields
  • Add success message when adding source
  • Clear scheduled hook when deactivate plugin
  • Convert HTML to WP blocks if possible
  • Redirect to source edit page when adding source
  • Bump & enforce minimum PHP version

1.0.1 – 2025-02-21

  • Initial release

upgrade_notice.2.2.0: Updates the database on the first request after the update. Sources, templates and imported posts are kept. Back up first, as for any update.

screenshots.caption: Add a source: the feed address and the parser are detected from the site URL, and the source test previews the items before anything is imported.
The Sources list: parser, last check, last item, categories, post status and the number of posts for each source, with views, filters and bulk actions.
Settings: update interval, sources per update, expiration delay and certificate path.
Parsers: seven built-in parsers, which you can duplicate as a starting point for your own JSON or XML parser.
The "Latest from your sources" block on a page: a three-column grid with each item's title linking to the original article, its source name, date and an excerpt.
The block's settings in the editor: number of items, sources, keyword filters, order, columns, image, source name, author, date and excerpt toggles, and the excerpt length.
